title: Moon Knight
subtitle: Marc Spector, from the early mysteries to the Midnight Mission.
intro: Start with From the Dead for a short introduction or The Midnight Mission for a longer modern run. Lemire and Smallwood reward some familiarity with Marc’s history.

modern.label: The Cosmic Circus · modern runs and chronology

classic.label: Crushing Krisis · choosing a starting point

stories.title: First appearances & Bad Moon Rising
stories.issues: Werewolf by Night (1972) #32–33; early guest stories; Moon Knight (1980) #1–4
stories.why: The historical starting point; early guest appearances lead into Marc’s solo title.
stories.match: Bad Moon Rising contains the first appearances and #1–4. Its catalog title only lists the solo issues, so the existing verified issue index establishes the earlier material.

stories.title: Moench & Sienkiewicz: Shadows of the Moon
stories.why: Continue the original run for the supporting cast and increasingly distinctive visual storytelling.
stories.match: This follows Bad Moon Rising. Read it before Final Rest.

stories.title: Final Rest & the first Black Spectre
stories.why: The final stretch of the first series, including a major recurring adversary.
stories.match: Final Rest covers #24–38; it continues the two earlier Epics.

stories.title: The Bottom
stories.why: A brutal modern relaunch. Choose it if you want the darker side of the character.
stories.match: Use Vol. 1: The Bottom. Midnight Sun (#7–13) is the next collection in the supplied catalog.

stories.title: From the Dead
stories.why: Six short adventures make an accessible introduction to modern Moon Knight and Mr. Knight.
stories.match: This is Ellis and Shalvey’s complete six-issue contribution; later volumes change creative teams.

stories.title: Lemire & Smallwood’s complete run
stories.why: A highly recommended exploration of Marc’s identities and history. Read after an introductory run if you want the references to land.
stories.match: These are alternative editions of #1–14. The catalog also has Lunatic, Reincarnations, and Birth and Death, which split the same run into three volumes.

stories.title: The Midnight Mission
stories.why: Jed MacKay’s neighborhood-focused relaunch is a practical entry into a longer modern story.
stories.match: Continue with Too Tough to Die (#7–12), Halfway to Sanity (#13–18), Road to Ruin (#19–24), and The Last Days of Moon Knight (#25–30); all are in the supplied catalog.
